title: Ultracentrifugal separation, characterization, and functional study of extracellular vesicles derived from serum-free cell culture
protocol: Grow suspension cell number in culture flask for FreeStyleTM 293-F cells to reach density of 0.6 – 1.0×10^6 cells/mL after 48 h.
Culture 2×10^5 cells/mL in a 125 mL polycarbonate, disposable, nonpyrogenic Erlenmeyer flask with final volume of 15–30 mL of FreeStyle 293 Expression Medium.
Maintain the culture in 37°C, 8% CO2 incubator with constant agitation on an orbital shaker rotating at 135 rpm.
Determine cell density and viability using trypan blue exclusion method.
Aliquot 100 μL of cell suspension into a microcentrifuge tube.
Add equal part of 0.4% trypan blue solution (100 μL) to the cell suspension to achieve 2 times dilution and mix completely.
Load 8 μL of the trypan blue/cell mixture to a hemocytometer chamber.
View the hemocytometer under light microscope with low magnification.
Count the stained (nonviable) cells from the four corner squares of hemocytometer.
Count the unstained (viable) cells from the four corner squares of hemocytometer.
Calculate the percentage of viable cells.
Calculate the cell density.
Use a minimum of 15 mL cell suspension at a density of 2×10^5 cells/mL as a starter culture.
Scale up or down the cell number based on experimental needs by modifying the culture volume.
Work in a sterilized biosafety cabinet for all transfection steps.
Aliquot 100 μL of cell suspension into microcentrifuge tube.
Determine cell viability using the trypan blue exclusion method.
Vortex the cell suspension vigorously at 2,500–3,000 rpm for about 30 seconds to dissociate clumping.
Count the cell number using a hemocytometer.
Pellet down the cells at 200 × g for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Resuspend the cells in fresh, pre-warmed medium.
For each 30 mL transfection, resuspend the cells in 28 mL of the medium.
Keep the cells in a culture flask under constant agitation to avoid cell clumping.
Dilute 30 μg of plasmid DNA or 72 μL of 20 μM siRNA in 1 mL Opti-MEM reduced-serum medium.
Dilute 60 μL of 293fectin in 1 mL Opti-MEM medium.
For plasmid DNA transfection, dilute 90 μL of 1 mg/mL PEI MAX in 1 mL Opti-MEM medium.
Incubate the diluted reagents for 5 minutes at 25°C.
Mix the solutions and incubate for 30 minutes at 25°C to allow formation of lipid-DNA or siRNA complex.
Add the complex to the previously prepared 28 mL cell suspension to form a total of 30 mL cell suspension culture.
Incubate the cells in a 37°C, 8% CO2 incubator with constant agitation on an orbital shaker rotating at 135 rpm for 48 h.
Collect the cell suspension in a 50 mL conical tube on Day 5.

Centrifuge the collected cell suspension twice at low speed (first at 1000 × g and then at 3000 × g, each for 10 min) to pellet down the cell body and eliminate cellular debris from the conditioned medium.
Observe the cell suspension under light microscopy.
Vortex the cell suspension vigorously at 2,500–3,000 rpm for about 30 seconds if clumping is observed.
Aliquot 100 μL of the cell suspension to a microcentrifuge tube for trypan blue exclusion assay and cell counting using hemocytometer.
Count both viable and dead cells in the sample.
Aliquot another 500 μL of cell suspension into a microcentrifuge tube for preparing WCL fraction.
Centrifuge the cell at 1,000 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes.
Discard the supernatant after centrifugation.
Resuspend the pellet in 1× sample buffer (dilute 5× sample buffer with ddH2O).
Pipette the WCL up and down several times to mix thoroughly.
Sonicate the lysate.
Sonicate the cell lysate for 30 seconds at an intensity of output 4.
Heat the sample at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Store the sample at -30°C for further analysis.
Centrifuge the cell suspension at 1,000 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes to pellet down the cell body.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 50 mL conical tube.
Centrifuge the supernatant at 3,000 × g at 4°C for 10 minutes to pellet down the cell debris.
Transfer the supernatant to another new 50 mL conical tube for EV fractionation.
Keep the conical tube on ice to avoid EV degradation.
Gently open the lid of the conical tube and carefully transfer the supernatant without disturbing the pellet.
Place the 50 mL conical tube containing l-EVs and s-EVs into the TOMY MX-307 high-speed refrigerated microcentrifuge.
Centrifuge the conditioned medium at 16,500 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C using the TOMY AR510-04 rotor (k-factor: 880; 13,500 rpm).
Remove the supernatant carefully to isolate the l-EV pellet.
Mark the position of the l-EV pellet on the conical tube.
Gently decant the supernatant containing s-EVs into a clean polycarbonate ultracentrifuge bottle while keeping the l-EV pellet intact in the original tube.
Resuspend the l-EV pellet in 500 μL sterile ice-cold filtered PBS.
Pipette up and down against the wall of the conical tube at the marking area to fully dislodge and dissociate the pellet.
Transfer the resuspended l-EV solution into a low-protein-binding microcentrifuge tube.
Add another 500 μL of sterile ice-cold PBS to the original conical tube and pipette against the wall to collect any remaining EVs.
Move the remaining EV suspension to a low-protein binding microcentrifuge tube to make a total of 1 mL l-EV resuspended in sterile ice-cold PBS.
Centrifuge the tube at 16,500 × g for 20 minutes at 4°C.
Pipette out 800 μL of the supernatant gently.
Leave approximately 200 μL of supernatant to avoid disturbing the pellet.
Centrifuge the tube again at 16,500 × g for 3 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the remaining supernatant completely.
Resuspend the pellet in a suitable buffer for downstream application.
Keep the tube on ice.
Aliquot 5–10 μL of l-EV suspension for NTA.
Dispense 3–5 μL for Qubit protein quantification assay.
Provide 10 μL for cell migration assay.
Supply 5–10 μL for lamellipodia formation assay.
Add 5× sample buffer to 1/4 of the sample volume for immunoblot analysis.
Weigh the polycarbonate ultracentrifuge bottles containing supernatant from step 13b.
Equate their weight by using sterile ice-cold PBS.
Place the balanced bottles into the pre-cooled Ti45 Beckman rotor.
Centrifuge the bottles at 120,000 × g for 70 min at 4°C (Ti45 Beckman Rotor; k-factor: 259; 32200 rpm).
Pull out the bottles from the rotor immediately after centrifugation.
Use a marker to circle the EV pellet.
Gently open the lid of the bottle.
Carefully decant the supernatant.
Wash the s-EV pellet with 400 μL sterile ice-cold PBS.
Gently resuspend the pellet by pipetting up and down several times.
Transfer the resuspended s-EV to a labeled, 1 mL open-top thick-wall polycarbonate ultracentrifuge tube placed on ice.
Weigh the tubes to ensure they are balanced.
Add sterile ice-cold PBS to equate their weight if necessary.
Place the tube into the pre-cold Beckman TLA120.2 fixed-angle rotor.
Centrifuge at 120,000 × g for 70 min at 4°C.
Immediately pull out the tube from the rotor and decant the supernatant.
Keep the pellet side of the tube facing upward during decanting.
Remove remaining medium in the tube completely by turning upside down on a paper towel.
Use p200 to remove residual medium if necessary.
Resuspend pellet in suitable buffer for downstream application.
Transfer EV suspension to low-protein-binding microcentrifuge tube (Watson, PK-15C-500).
Keep tube on ice.
Dispense 5–10 μL of s-EV suspension for NTA.
Dispense 3–5 μL for Qubit protein quantification assay.
Dispense 10 μL for cell migration assay.
Dispense 5–10 μL for lamellipodia formation assay.
Add 5× sample buffer to 1/4 of the sample volume for immunoblot analysis.
Store s-EVs suspended in PBS at -80°C for later use.
Quantify the protein concentration of l-EV and s-EV fractions using QubitTM protein quantification assay.
Add 0.2% SDS to the EVs suspension to lyse the EVs for measuring internal protein amount.
Prepare 3 QubitTM assay tubes for standards and 1 tube for each sample.
Label the tubes according to their orders at the tube lids only.
Dilute the QubitTM reagent in the buffer in a ratio of 1:200.
Vortex the working solution for 5-10 seconds to mix well.
Dispense 1–5 μL of EV samples suspended in sterile PBS into a Qubit assay tube.
Dilute the EV samples with QubitTM working solution to a total volume of 200 μL.
Dispense 10 μL of each standard #1, #2, and #3 into clean tubes.
Add an equal volume of PBS (1–5 μL) used for loading the samples to each standard tube.
Dilute the standards with QubitTM working solution to a total volume of 200 μL.
Vortex all tubes for 2–3 seconds to mix well.
Incubate the tubes at 25°C for 15 minutes.
Warm up the QubitTM working solution to around 25°C before measurement.
Insert the tube into the QubitTM Fluorometer and take the reading.
Dilute the EVs sample in 300–500 μL of sterile ice-cold PBS and keep on ice.
Clean the LM10 viewing unit using a deionized-water-dampened optical lens grade cleaning tissue to wipe over the inside surface of the top-plate window and the optical plate surface.
Dry the surface by wiping with the tissue and blowing with an air stream from an air compressor.
Assemble the LM10 viewing unit and attach the power lead.
Rinse the beam path twice by injecting 1 mL of PBS into the chamber slowly using a syringe.
Vortex the EV sample gently at 500–1,000 rpm for 5 s.
Withdraw 0.5 ml of sample with a 1 mL syringe ensuring no bubbles are introduced.
Introduce the sample slowly and steadily into the chamber.
Withdraw the sample by pulling the plunger and then introduce it again.
Repeat these steps three times to distribute the sample evenly in the chamber.
Add more PBS to resuspend EVs and pipette up and down several times.
Gently vortex the suspension at 500–1,000 rpm for 10–15 s if aggregates are visible.
Capture a movie of particles under Brownian motion for 30–60 seconds.
Change to a different observation field by slowly injecting more sample into the chamber.
Record another movie and repeat this step four times to capture five movies in total.
Adjust the detection threshold so that most particles are properly identified.
Proceed with NTA analysis to determine particle concentration and size distribution.
Add one-fourth volume of 5× sample buffer into the l-EV and s-EV samples to make 1× sample buffer concentration.
Heat the samples at 95°C for 5 min.
Load equal cell number, equal protein concentration, and equal EV number per sample onto SDS-PAGE.
For cell-number normalization, load 1×10^4 cells for WCL and 4×10^6 cells for EVs.
For total-protein normalization, load 500 ng of protein.
For EV-number normalization, load 6×10^8 EVs.
Run the SDS-PAGE and resolve proteins based on size.
Transfer resolved proteins onto polyvinylidene difluoride (PVDF) membrane using a semi-dry western blot transfer system for 45 min to 1 hour at 24 V.
Block the membrane in 20 mL of 5% skim milk/PBS-0.05% Tween 20 solution and rock it on a shaker for 1 hour at 25°C.
Wash the membrane with PBS-T once.
Incubate the membrane in primary antibody diluted in PBS-T/0.01% NaN3 and rock it for 12–16 hours at 4°C.
Wash the membrane with PBS-T for 10 minutes at 25°C, repeating three times.
Incubate the membrane with AP- or HRP-labeled secondary antibody diluted in PBS-T for 1 hour at 25°C.
Wash the membrane with PBS-T for 10 min at 25°C.
Repeat step 3 times.
For AP detection, wash the membrane with AP buffer at 25°C once.
Dilute 37.5 μL BCIP solution (50 mg/mL in dimethylformamide) and 50 μL NBT solution (100 mg/mL in 70% dimethylformamide) in 10 mL AP buffer.
Add 4–5 mL of diluted solution to each membrane and shake at 25°C until the protein bands appear.
To stop the reaction, discard the solution.
Wash the membrane with tap water.
Dry the membrane.
Quantify the signals using ImageJ software.
For HRP detection, add 5 mL of ECL Prime western blotting detection reagents.
Detect chemiluminescence using an image detector such as LAS 4000 (GE Healthcare).
Seed 293-F cells suspended in 1.2 mL of FreeStyle 293 Expression Medium containing EVs in 3.5 cm culture dishes.
Incubate the seeded cells on CytoSMART Lux2 apparatus in an 8% CO2 incubator at 37°C.
Take pictures of the cells every 15 minutes for 48 hours after a 30-minute acclimation period.
Track the migration of cells manually by ImageJ using Cell Tracker plug-ins such as MTrackJ or Manual Tracking.
Select 10 cells per region and track cell migration every 15 minutes for 48 hours.
Calculate the average migration speed for every 12 hours.
Compare the calculated speeds with the first 12 hours migration speed.
Suspend HEK 293-F cells (8×10^3 cells) in 0.1 mL of FreeStyle 293 Expression Medium.
Seed the suspended cells in glass-based dishes and incubate them in an 8% CO2 incubator at 37°C for 3 hours.
Replace the FreeStyle 293 Expression Medium with fresh medium containing EVs.
Incubate the cells with the new medium at 37°C, 8% CO2 for 15 minutes.
Fix the cells with 4% (wt/vol) paraformaldehyde in FreeStyle 293 Expression Medium at 25°C for 5 minutes.
Wash the fixed cells with tris-buffered saline once.
Permeabilize the cells with 0.1% Triton X-100 in 1% bovine serum albumin/TBS for 5 minutes.
Wash the permeabilized cells with TBS once.
Block the cells with 3% (wt/vol) BSA in TBS at 4°C for 16 h.
Wash the cells with TBS once.
Incubate the cells with anti-WAVE2 antibody or an antibody to any other lamellipodia localizing protein in 1% BSA/TBS (90 μL) at 25°C for 2 h.
Wash the cells 3 times with TBS.
Incubate cells with secondary fluorochrome-labeled antibodies and fluorochrome-labeled phalloidin in 1% BSA/TBS at 25°C for 1 h.
Wash the cells 3 times with TBS.
Soak the cells in TBS containing 0.02% (w/v) NaN3.
Observe cells under a confocal microscope.
Lysate l-EVs prepared from 3.6×10^7 cells in 300 μl of lysis buffer (containing protease inhibitors) on ice.
Centrifuge lysed l-EVs at 14,000 × g for 5 min at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to GST-PAK1-PBD-conjugated resin and rotate at 4°C for 45 min.
Wash the resin three times with 0.5 ml of lysis buffer.
Analyze proteins bound to resin by immunoblotting.
